title: POP signal-fusion chooser: p50/p95 + network-health scoring with model-variant fallback
creator: Asha Varma
description: Replace the simple percentile-based pop chooser with a signal-fusion arbiter that combines p50/p95 latency telemetry and network-health signals (packet loss, retransmits, jitter) to produce a single numeric score per POP. Use that score to choose preferred region/tier and, when needed, trigger an automated fallback to a compatible model variant (e.g., quantized or smaller model) with graceful degradation and cooldown. Goal: reduce P95 SLO breaches during transient network degradations while preserving unit-cost objectives and avoiding unnecessary cross-region failovers.
acceptance_criteria: New chooser produces a single pop score (0..100) computed from p50, p95, packet-loss, and EWMA stability; documented formula in design doc
Traffic routing shows reduced cross-pop thrash during short-lived packet-loss spikes (sim replay test: <10% routing change for events <90s)
Automated fallback to model-variant triggers only when score falls below threshold and kept active with defined hysteresis; canary rollout shows no increased error rate
Console dashboards display score, contributing signals, and decision timeline for every routed request
New algorithm covered by unit tests, integration tests in staging, and a canary run with rollback hooks defined
progress_updates: 2025-11-21: Spike evaluation—collected 30 days of p50/p95 and network metrics from 6 primary POPs; initial normalization factors computed
2025-11-24: Prototype scoring function (weighted z-scores with clip) implemented; local sim running against historical incidents; P95 improvements ~18% in sims
2025-11-28: Built EWMA smoothing for p95 and packet-loss (1min/15min) and added variance penalty to avoid flip-flops
2025-11-30: Implemented model-variant selection rules (preferredVariant, fallbackVariant, compatibility table) and cooldown state machine
2025-12-02: Integration tests green in staging; prepping canary config and runbook for rollout
comments: Liam O'Connor: Please add a short note about how this interacts with reserved capacity routing (Dedicated). We must ensure we don't route Dedicated customers to Hosted fallbacks.
Diego Morales: Fine-tune weight on p50 vs p95; in busy POPs p95 matters more for tail latency-sensitive customers—propose 0.6 p95, 0.25 p50, 0.1 packet-loss, 0.05 jitter as starting point.
PM feedback (Maya Chen): Make sure console exposes both the raw signals and the computed score with an explanation (why we routed to X POP).
Security review (TBD): Need to confirm that telemetry exposures in logs don't leak customer prompt hashes; only expose aggregated metrics and request IDs
test_plan: Unit tests for score components (normalization, clipping, weighting)
Replay test: feed 7 days of production traces with injected packet-loss to validate stability
Staging canary: route 5% of traffic for 24h with monitoring and automated rollback scripts
Load test: ensure scorer adds <3ms median CPU overhead per request at 10k rps
rollout_plan: Canary-1: 5% traffic (non-enterprise customers) for 24h; ops on-call notified
Canary-2: 25% traffic for 48h if metrics stable
Ramp to 50% and then 100% over a week while monitoring P95 / SLO errors
Immediate rollback triggers: P95 increase >15% vs baseline OR error-rate increase >1% absolute
Post-rollout: 30-day observation window with trend analysis and cost impact report
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive fallbacks increase unit cost (more expensive variants). Mitigation: cost penalty included in scoring and a budget throttle per customer tier.
Risk: Flip-flop routing due to noisy p50/p95 signals. Mitigation: EWMA smoothing, variance penalty, and minimum hold time (hysteresis).
Risk: Interference with Dedicated routing. Mitigation: Scoped chooser respects capacity tags and Dedicated affinity before applying fallbacks.
dependencies: ENG-97210 - telemetry ingestion: add retransmit/packet-loss metrics to Pop telemetry
notes: Scoring function is intentionally conservative: thresholds chosen to prefer staying in-pop and switching to a quantized fallback variant before cross-pop failover. We will revisit weights after canary and collect feedback from Solutions Eng on enterprise behavior.
